Q: TailwindCSS for beginners A:

tailwindcss is a pretty good tool but not for beginners, Not in the sense that it is hard, but in the sense that it does a small abstraction (hides some details from you) in the process of allowing you to write code faster. This is a positive thing to do when you're coding and you know what the details that are being removed are AND can do them manually.
But it is a negative when you're trying to learn, as you need to feel the pain of dealing with the details with your goal is to be proficient in the tools you are using.

Q: Do I still need to use break after I use return in switch/case? A:

return terminates your function, so the code won't continue executing (and potentially falling through to the next case block). There's no point in using break in such a situation.

Q: How to retrieve all paths of a source node without a target node using networkx A:

You can add a dummy source and sink, call them "s" and "t", then add edges from "s" to all nodes with indegree 0, and add edges from all nodes with outdegree 0 to "t". Then enumerate all simple paths between "s" and "t".

Q: R software, making boxplot, need finite 'ylim' value A:

I think it would be easy if you could give a glimpse of the subset BM. This error mostly appears when your data is empty. In your case, there is a high chance that your olympic dataset doesn't have "basketball" sport or doesn't have "M" gender, which leads to an empty data frame after subsetting. let's reproduce this scenario.

when olympic has basketball sport for Men ("M")

sample data

olympic <- data.frame(
  sport = c("basketball", "basketball", "swimming", "basketball", "swimming", "basketball"),
  sex = c("M", "F", "M", "M", "F", "M"),
  height = c(210, 180, 185, 198, 165, 215)
)

## select the subset
BM <- subset(olympic, sport == "basketball" & sex == "M")
## A glimpse of the data
print(BM)

which gives:

       sport sex height
1 basketball   M    210
4 basketball   M    198
6 basketball   M    215

This way graphing works

## graph a boxplot of heights
boxplot(BM$height)

when olympic has no basketball sport for Men ("M")

olympic <- data.frame(
  sport = c("basketball", "basketball", "swimming", "basketball", "swimming", "basketball"),
  sex = c("F", "F", "F", "F", "F", "F"),
  height = c(210, 180, 185, 198, 165, 215)
)

BM <- subset(olympic, sport == "basketball" & sex == "M")
print(BM)

which gives an empty dataframe

[1] sport  sex    height
<0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

graphing leads to the error:

boxplot(BM$height)
Error in plot.window(xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim, log = log, yaxs = pars$yaxs) : 
  need finite 'ylim' values
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In min(x) : no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf
2: In max(x) : no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf
